text:
**Chase UK is better for cashback. For savings it depends on the type of account and how much you want to lock away.** The sources I found don't all agree on some rates, so check the apps before you commit.

## Cashback: Chase wins
- Chase pays 2% cashback (up to £20 a month) and 5% on round-ups.
- There are conditions. You need 15 or more card or Direct Debit payments in the month and £1,000 or more across Chase savers every day. Cashback is paid the following month.
- It only applies to set categories: groceries, restaurants and cafes, takeaways, transport, fuel and public EV charging.
- I didn't find a standard everyday cashback on Monzo's current account. As far as I know, Monzo only offers occasional targeted partner offers. I didn't verify that in this search, so check the app.

## Savings: it depends

**Easy access (instant withdrawals)**
- Chase's standard Chase Saver was 2.50% AER variable from 12 November 2026.
- New Chase customers can get a boosted rate if they open it within their first 31 days. One source puts the total at 4.75% including a 2.25% boost for 12 months. Others quote 4.5%, probably because they were written before the 12 November rate change.
- Monzo's Instant Access rate depends on your plan. It runs from 2.80% AER on the free plan to 3.80% on Max. Those figures come from Monzo's help page, which is flagged as old. A tracker gave similar free-plan rates in November.
- Chase is clearly ahead for new customers during the boost. After the boost ends, Chase's 2.50% is slightly below Monzo's free-plan 2.80%.

**Regular saver**
- Chase offers a fixed 6.50% AER for 12 months on up to £300 a month. That's the highest headline rate in this comparison. Because you pay in monthly, you only earn it on part of the money at any time.
- Monzo's equivalent is its 2026 Saving Challenge. It pays 5% AER (variable) but only on the paid plans, Extra, Perks or Max.

**Fixed rate (money locked away)**
- Monzo's fixed-rate pots are 5.25% AER for 3 years, 5.10% for 2 years and 4.70% for 1 year. I didn't find a comparable fixed-term product at Chase.

## Which to pick
- **Chase:** you're a new customer, you spend on groceries, fuel and transport, and you're happy to keep £1,000 or more in savings. Together that gives you the best cashback and the best easy-access rate for the first year.
- **Monzo:** you want fixed-rate bonds, a Cash ISA, or an all-in-one app. Its paid plans also lift the savings rates.
- **Both:** many people use Chase for cashback and its savings, and keep Monzo for budgeting and pots.

Neither is the top payer on the market. One source says Chase's saver rate is still 0.51% behind the category leader at 5.26%. If you only want the best rate, it's worth checking a comparison table too.

I'm not a financial adviser, and these rates are variable and change often.
